A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same X-hacking study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, and retained experiments can be matched reliably across the reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original AutoML/SHAP experiments on 23 classification datasets and synthetic noise/redundancy experiments, with additional results in Appendices B–D.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds original Bayesian-versus-random directed-search experiments and time-to-first-success measurements in Sections 5.2 and 5.4 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: V1 presents post-hoc selection, weighted-sum optimization and a small Optuna simulation. V3 adds an implemented distributed directed-search procedure combining auto-sklearn's search space, Optuna's MOTPESampler and Ray Tune to jointly maximize accuracy and minimize mean absolute SHAP. Weighted-sum scalarization remains an alternative in Appendix C.

E1.justification: The same 23 binary-classification datasets appear in v1 Table 1 and v3 Table 5, and the original synthetic noise/redundancy scenarios are retained. Targeting four features per dataset in the new search experiments changes experimental settings, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds random sampling as an evaluated comparator for Bayesian directed search under matched budgets, and directly compares directed search with post-hoc cherry-picking for search time. The default random-forest reference remains. Appendix A's AutoML capability survey does not constitute additional experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The retained post-hoc study still uses a one-hour search, 100-second candidate limit and 20% test split. V3 adds 12-hour directed searches targeting four features per dataset, totaling 92 targets, with one-hour candidate limits and matched Bayesian/random budgets. Section 5.4 additionally evaluates first success within one hour.

E4.justification: V3 adds a controlled optimizer substitution—Bayesian versus random search—to assess the benefit of guidance, together with convergence-over-time and time-to-first-success analyses. It also identifies targets for which searches fail within the allotted budget. The earlier noise/redundancy sensitivity experiments and SHAP-slope diagnostics are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify random seed 42. Neither reports repeated independent runs, confidence intervals or significance tests for the experimental comparisons. V3's additional convergence curves and summaries across features do not change this uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V3 adds Bayesian/random convergence results across 92 feature targets, reports 20/92 targets without a defensible model, and supplies first-success times for 15 datasets. Table 1 includes 3 seconds for breast-w and 55 minutes 18 seconds for credit-g. These are new results under new protocols; the earlier post-hoc and simulation findings are retained.

T1.justification: Sections 3–4 add formal definitions of the searched model sets and their confirmatory Rashomon intersection. The scalarization also changes its sign reference from the baseline model in v1 Equation 2 to the best-performing model in v3 Appendix C, and revises the weight prescription. No theorem or proof is added; the simulation-generating equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: V3 elevates the custom directed-search implementation and its efficiency comparisons to principal contributions. Its abstract claims threefold acceleration over random sampling, and its introduction claims tenfold acceleration over post-hoc selection. V1 claims feasibility and proposes greater efficiency without these quantitative comparisons; the original redundancy-related claim remains.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly relates vulnerability to predictive multiplicity, interprets unsuccessful finite searches as evidence of robustness, and restricts operational defensibility to predictive performance. It adds preregistration guidance covering AutoML search spaces while removing much of v1's domain-standard and audacity discussion. The core redundancy explanation and absence of observed real-world misuse remain.

D1.justification: Appendices B and D document search-space extraction through ConfigSpace, Optuna/Ray integration, trial storage, algorithm and hyperparameter inventories, and directed-search resources of up to 292 CPUs and 1 TB RAM. The retained post-hoc resources remain 192 CPUs and 300 GB. The cited replication repository changes from Selbosh/p-hacking to datasciapps/x-hacking.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning around model multiplicity, underspecification and Rashomon sets, citing works such as Black et al., Brunet et al., Fisher et al. and D'Amour et al. It claims to extend model-family studies to complete analysis pipelines and adds an extensive AutoML capability survey, replacing much of v1's broader research-misconduct background.

P1.justification: The background and introduction are extensively rewritten. V3 separates the problem statement, methods and experiments, removes the standalone misconduct taxonomy and audacity subsection, moves scalarization into Appendix C, and reorganizes the experimental appendices. An impact statement is also added. These are substantial narrative changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column main-text layout and substantially resizes and relocates existing displays. It adds timing, capability and implementation tables, an architecture diagram, and directed-search convergence plots. Retained simulation scatterplots gain axis labels, while the original appendix's post-hoc plot images are preserved under new numbering.

improvement.justification: V1 lacked a real-data evaluation of its directed-search proposal. V3 addresses this with matched-budget Bayesian/random comparisons across 92 feature targets and substantially fuller implementation documentation, strengthening empirical support and reproducibility. The exact speedup claims remain underqualified: the reported timing summaries do not directly establish threefold acceleration, repeated-run uncertainty is absent, and post-hoc versus directed-search resource limits differ. These limitations constrain the quantitative claims but do not outweigh the substantial gain in evidence for the directed-search approach.
